about.metaDescription: Origin, method, and the inflection at day twenty-three. Built inside CognitiveLab at WelloWork AB.

hero.lede: TwentyThird is a psychodynamic AI for self‑discovery. It maps the recurring loops and structures beneath the symptom — language, attachment, repetition — and returns a working brief, not a quiz.

row.headingPost: proposed in a letter, kept as figure.
row.para1: The 23-day cycle was Wilhelm Fliess's hypothesis, argued through his correspondence with Freud at the close of the nineteenth century. Contemporary science does not support fixed biorhythms.
row.para2: We keep the number for what it names — the threshold at which curiosity matures into awareness. Day‑23 is figure, not biology.

origin.headingItalic: Answered a question we kept being asked

row.para1: TwentyThird began inside the CognitiveLab at WelloWork AB, where the team was developing cognitive training systems. Friends and colleagues began bringing personal questions — anxiety, recurring patterns, the loops they could not name.
row.para2: Between clinical practice as physicians, the pilot data we were accumulating, and a long reading list in psychoanalysis and Lacanian theory, we had something to offer. TwentyThird is what that became.

row.para1: TwentyThird performs root-cause analysis. It maps the subconscious loop across years, reads the linguistic unconscious in word choice and slips of speech, surfaces attachment at the intimacy threshold, and writes a working plan for shadow work.
row.para2: The output is therapist-ready. Names the structure, not the surface.

philosophy.sub1: We do root‑cause analysis. By fusing the foundational insights of Sigmund Freud with Jacques Lacan's breakthroughs in linguistics, desire, and identity.
philosophy.sub2: Most tools work on the surface. We work where it was written — in the architecture of language, the slips of speech, the patterns you have not yet named.

privacy.lede: Confidentiality is not a feature here; it is the precondition for depth. People speak freely only where they feel safe — so the room is built to keep what you say protected.
privacy.rowBody: The work asks for your most undefended material. The room is built to receive it in confidence and keep it closed to anyone it was not meant for.
privacy.listProtectionVal: Held under the highest‑grade protection available.
privacy.footVal: a quiet, secure place to speak deeply

process.lede: Communication deepens in four moves. Each one widens what the system can read — from a single intake to a standing conversation.
process.step1Body: Create your account and complete a 10‑step intake. This is the deep‑core profiling pass; the first reading is built entirely from what you set down here.
process.step2Body: Add the people who shape you, each by role — partner, closest friend, parent, sibling, co‑parent. What they share is never visible to you; what you share is never visible to them. Only the system reads both.
process.step3Body: On Sunday evenings, tell us what happened during your week and how it felt to live it. Each Catchup refines the reading — the picture sharpens as the weeks accumulate.
process.step4Body: Speak in a fully private consultation with the analyst — a voice that knows you better than anyone, trained across 23 layers of frontier AI models.

brain.state1Body: We track the recurring cycles in your choices, relationship anxieties, and emotional triggers. By identifying these loops, we show you exactly where your conscious intentions are being hijacked by unconscious programming.
brain.state2Body: Move past superficial personality quizzes. This is a structural scan of your psychological dynamics — mapping how your past experiences shape your current identity, ego, and defense mechanisms.
brain.state3Body: Rooted in Lacanian theory, our AI analyzes your word associations, pauses, and speech patterns. We help you read between the lines of your own thoughts to access the hidden anxieties and desires you haven't yet been able to voice.

transform.lede: Three movements in the work. Three places where insight becomes change.
transform.row1Body: The same attractor draws you toward the same kind of person, the same fight, the same withdrawal. We surface the pattern across years, name it, and watch it lose its gravity.
transform.row2Body: Your dreams are rehearsals of meaning. We follow their grammar — the displacements, the condensations, the slips — back to the waking decision they were trying to make for you.
transform.row2Dream1Pre: I am back in my parents' house
transform.row2Dream1Mid: , but the rooms keep opening into other rooms
transform.row2Dream2Pre: A man with my father's voice
transform.row2Dream2Mid: hands me a key. The key turns into water
transform.row2Dream3Pre: I wake before I can open the door
transform.row3Body: The ceiling you keep hitting is rarely about skill. It is a script — written early, rehearsed quietly — that we will help you read aloud and rewrite, sentence by sentence.

outcomes.lede: Data-driven self-awareness, delivered in the language of a clinician — not a quiz.
outcomes.row1Body: What used to take a relationship of many years can now begin with weeks of preparation. Walk into your therapist's office knowing what you're there to say.
outcomes.row2Body: A structural diagram of you — exportable, shareable, deeply intelligible to a trained clinician. Not a personality quiz; a working brief.
outcomes.row3Body: Daily prompts and rituals that take the insight off the page and into the body. Small, deliberate. Built around your structure, not a generic curriculum.
outcomes.row3PromptPost: to be seen? And what were you keeping safe by hiding?

hero.lede: Therapy works. It also takes time to know what you're there for. TwentyThird compresses the preparation — the part where you learn what you're actually saying — so the room itself can go faster.

compression.body1: Therapy is not the place to figure out the question. It is the place to live with it. The compression we offer is on the approach — the months a clinician usually spends listening for the shape of the brief.
compression.body2: Across the pilot cohort, prepared subjects reached working alliance in fewer sessions. The reading was already there.

hero.lede: Naming a pattern is only the first move. The plan is the second — daily prompts and small rituals built around your structure, not a generic curriculum.

week.lede: Reflective, embodied, written. The week breathes around the pattern the report named, not around a curriculum.

mon.prompt: “Where today did you choose not to be seen?”

tue.prompt: “Take a walk without an errand. Note one thing you almost said.”

wed.prompt: “What did you over-qualify today, and what was the unqualified sentence underneath?”

thu.prompt: “A body scan from the throat down. Where does the holding live?”

fri.prompt: “Write the sentence you would have said if you were already allowed.”

sat.prompt: “A long walk. No prompts. Notice what the silence brings back.”

sun.prompt: “Read the week back. Which line was already true?”

adaptation.rowHeadingLead: Last week’s recurrence sets next week’s
adaptation.body: When the pattern strength drops, the prompts thin. When a pattern surges, the prompts return. The aim is not adherence. The aim is the smallest scaffolding the structure still needs.

shadow.rowHeadingLead: The deliberate practice of speaking what was
shadow.body: Shadow work, in this context, is not exposure. It is not a purge. It is the slow practice of saying — to oneself, first — what one had been taught to keep unsaid. Three before / after lines drawn from real plans.

r1.next: I have not yet practised wanting it aloud.

r2.old: I should be over this by now.
r2.next: the timeline I borrowed was not for this kind of grief.

r3.next: I am exactly the volume the room was not built for.

frame.body1: A curriculum is a set of moves a stranger built. A structure is the shape your particular life happens to take. The plan is built against the latter. Every prompt is anchored to a line in your report — when the line dissolves, the prompt does too.
frame.body2: Nothing here is supposed to be permanent. The plan is rented. The structure is yours.

metadata.title: The science — TwentyThird
metadata.description: A century of psychoanalytic theory and four decades of empirical research into pattern, language, and the unconscious.

hero.lede: TwentyThird is built on a century of psychoanalytic theory and four decades of empirical research into pattern, language, and the unconscious. This is what we read, and why.

lineages.lede: Two readings of the unconscious, a half-century apart. Together they form the spine of the method.

freud.body1: Freud's lasting contribution is structural, not thematic. The dynamic unconscious is not a basement of forgotten content — it is a working organ of the mind, rehearsing, repeating, transferring.
freud.body2: We read him as a clinician of repetition. The same scene arrives in different decades. That recurrence is the signal the model is trained to find.

lacan.headlineLead: The unconscious is structured like a
lacan.body1Lead: Lacan's reading shifts the field. The signifier moves; meaning slides along chains of metonymy and metaphor. The mirror stage names the founding misrecognition.
lacan.body1Italic: Desire is the desire of the Other.
lacan.body2: In our pipeline this is concrete. We read dreams and waking speech as text — the displacements, condensations, and slips carry the structuring grammar.

research.lede: Five converging strands from attachment, narrative, and process research. Not a complete bibliography — the anchors the model actually rests on.

limits.claim1Strong: We are not a substitute for a therapist.
limits.claim1Body: The model prepares the conversation. It does not hold it.
limits.claim2Strong: We are not a diagnostic instrument under DSM or ICD.
limits.claim2Body: The categories we work in are structural — obsessional, hysterical, phobic — not nosological. They name how a person is organised, not what they have.
limits.claim3Body: The number comes from Wilhelm Fliess's correspondence with Freud at the end of the nineteenth century. Contemporary science does not support fixed biorhythms. We keep the number for what it names — the inflection from curiosity into awareness.

subconscious-loops.subtitle: subconscious loops
subconscious-loops.definition: Repeating sequences of feeling, action, and outcome that occur outside conscious choice. Naming the loop is the first interruption of it.
subconscious-loops.seedReading: approaches closeness then engineers a small failure to step back.
subconscious-loops.seedTakeaway: the retreat is the loop. not the closeness.

linguistic-unconscious.subtitle: linguistic unconscious
linguistic-unconscious.definition: The way unconscious material surfaces in word choice, repetition, slips, and the structure of speech — Lacan's claim that the unconscious is structured like a language.
linguistic-unconscious.seedReading: speech doubles on the word “should” — site of an inherited demand.
linguistic-unconscious.seedTakeaway: someone else's voice is still speaking through this word.

father-imago.subtitle: father‑imago
father-imago.definition: The internalized image of the father, formed early and partly mythic. It shapes how authority, ambition, and judgment are met later in life.
father-imago.seedReading: judges from above before being judged from above — the position is identical.
father-imago.seedTakeaway: the seat changes. the chair does not.

intimacy-threshold.subtitle: intimacy threshold
intimacy-threshold.definition: The point at which closeness begins to feel like a risk, and a defensive move follows. Different for each person; surprisingly stable across relationships.
intimacy-threshold.seedReading: holds well until the other becomes legible — then withdraws.
intimacy-threshold.seedTakeaway: being known is the edge, not being close.

desire-structure.subtitle: desire structure
desire-structure.definition: What the user actually wants, distinguished from what they have been told to want. Often discovered by negation — by noticing what they refuse.
desire-structure.seedReading: names many wants, refuses two — the refusal is the signal.
desire-structure.seedTakeaway: what is pushed away points more clearly than what is chased.

professional-block.subtitle: professional block
professional-block.definition: Where work catches: the start, the middle, the finish, or the visibility. Each location has its own unconscious source.
professional-block.seedReading: the finish line is where the doubt arrives, never the start.
professional-block.seedTakeaway: the block is at visibility, not at effort.

mother-imago.subtitle: mother‑imago
mother-imago.definition: The internalized image of the mother — the first attunement, the first separation. It informs the texture of dependence and refuge.
mother-imago.seedReading: too early to say with confidence — the shape is forming.
mother-imago.seedTakeaway: early attunement leaves a long signature.

dream-logic.subtitle: dream logic
dream-logic.definition: The condensation and displacement at work in dream material. Read for the grammar, not the symbols.
dream-logic.seedReading: too early to say with confidence — the shape is forming.
dream-logic.seedTakeaway: dream content has its own grammar.

relational-pattern.subtitle: relational pattern
relational-pattern.definition: The recurring posture taken in relationships — pursuer, withdrawer, parent, child, equal. Stable across partners more than the partners are stable across the user.
relational-pattern.seedReading: too early to say with confidence — the shape is forming.
relational-pattern.seedTakeaway: the same shape appears across different rooms.

defenses.subtitle: defenses
defenses.definition: The characteristic moves used to keep difficult material out of awareness — intellectualization, displacement, reaction formation, splitting. Defenses are not failures; they are old solutions.
defenses.seedReading: too early to say with confidence — the shape is forming.
defenses.seedTakeaway: the defense names what was once unbearable.

shadow.subtitle: shadow
shadow.definition: What has been disowned and assigned to others — the qualities the user is most certain they are not. Often the route to vitality.
shadow.seedReading: too early to say with confidence — the shape is forming.

transference.subtitle: transference
transference.definition: The way old relational figures are projected onto present ones — the analyst, the partner, the boss. The pattern reveals the imago.
transference.seedReading: too early to say with confidence — the shape is forming.
transference.seedTakeaway: old figures arrive in present rooms.

consulting.previewTurnAnalyst2: The morning is the verdict, not the trial. Your intimacy threshold rehearsed leaving weeks before the conversation.
consulting.offerLede: A long-form sitting with the analyst, held in the same voice as your readings. Sessions are private, kept in the case file, and feed the readings between sittings.
consulting.offerPanel1Body: The analyst will name what's happening in your speech — the slip, the qualifier, the half-said — and hold it there until you can see it.
consulting.offerPanel2Body: Every sitting is written down. The next reading reads it. Patterns surface across weeks, not turns.
consulting.offerPanel3Body: Not a chatbot rotation. A single analytic voice, trained on your intake and refined by every catchup.
consulting.offerFootLine: Subscribers receive one clinical report each month.
consulting.previewRailAria: case file areas the analyst is reading from
consulting.previewBubble1: I keep ending things the week they get serious. I don't know why I do it.
consulting.previewAnalyst1: You name a pattern, then narrate it as a stranger's. The “I don't know” is doing work — it keeps the act on the far side of intention. Notice when the withdrawal begins. Often the foreclosure happens earlier than the leaving.
consulting.previewBubble2: Earlier how? Last time it felt like I just woke up one morning and knew.
consulting.previewAnalyst2: The morning is the verdict, not the trial. Your intimacy threshold reading from week 04 noted the same shape — a quiet rehearsal of leaving, two to three weeks before the conversation. The morning is when the body finally agrees with what you'd already decided.
consulting.previewBubble3: That's the part that scares me. That it's already decided.
consulting.previewAnalyst3: Decided is the word. Not chosen. Something in the structure prefers the foreclosure to the test. We will keep going there.

q1_1.title: Which words best describe the home you grew up in.
q1_1.subtitle: pick up to three words that feel true, even if they contradict each other — homes are usually a mix

q1_2.title: As a child, what role did you naturally take.
q1_2.subtitle: think about the part you played in your family without anyone telling you to — the peacemaker, the helper, the quiet one

q1_3.title: How emotionally safe did you feel growing up.
q1_3.subtitle: go with your gut feeling about the home, not the version the family would tell a stranger

q1_4.title: Were emotions openly discussed at home.
q1_4.subtitle: not just whether feelings were there, but whether anyone actually named or talked about them out loud

q1_5.title: One memory from childhood that still feels emotionally alive today.
q1_5.subtitle: describe one specific scene that still comes back to you — where you were, who was there, what happened, how it felt

q1_6.title: What did you learn you had to do to receive love or approval.
q1_6.subtitle: the small things you noticed worked — being good, being quiet, achieving, staying out of the way — share what you remember adjusting

q1_7.title: What emotions were difficult to express in your home.
q1_7.subtitle: which feelings got ignored, dismissed, or punished when you tried to show them — anger, sadness, fear, joy, anything

q1_8.title: When you think about your younger self, what do you feel toward them.
q1_8.subtitle: be honest about the feeling that comes up — warmth, sadness, distance, frustration, protectiveness — whatever is actually there

q2_1.title: How would you describe your mother or primary maternal caregiver.
q2_1.subtitle: a few sentences about what she was like, how she showed up for you, and how you felt around her

q2_2.title: How would you describe your father or primary paternal caregiver.
q2_2.subtitle: a few sentences about what he was like, how he showed up for you, and how you felt around him

q2_3.title: Your sibling position.
q2_3.subtitle: where you fell in the order — oldest, middle, youngest, only child, or somewhere in between

q2_4.title: Which role best fits your sibling position.
q2_4.subtitle: beyond birth order, the role you ended up playing — the responsible one, the rebel, the invisible one, the favourite

q2_5.title: Which parent understood you best.
q2_5.subtitle: name them and say what they saw in you that the other one missed or got wrong

q2_6.title: Which parent influenced your fears the most.
q2_6.subtitle: whose worries you absorbed growing up, and how those fears still show up in your life today

q2_7.title: What did conflict look like in your family.
q2_7.subtitle: describe the shape arguments took — yelling, silence, slammed doors, cold weeks, repeated patterns — whatever felt familiar

q2_8.title: What kind of attention felt hardest to receive.
q2_8.subtitle: the kind of care that made you uncomfortable — praise, concern, physical closeness, being seen — and why it was hard

q3_1.title: How religious or spiritual was the environment you grew up in.
q3_1.subtitle: the actual atmosphere of the home — practices, rules, beliefs in the air — not what you believe now as an adult

q3_2.title: Which message was strongest growing up.
q3_2.subtitle: the rule or expectation repeated so often it became background noise — about success, behaviour, image, duty, family

q3_3.title: How strongly do you feel judged by society.
q3_3.subtitle: how much you feel watched or evaluated by people outside your close circle — at work, online, in public

q3_4.title: What beliefs from your upbringing still shape you.
q3_4.subtitle: the values, rules, or assumptions you inherited and still live by, even if you haven't thought about them in years

q3_5.title: Which beliefs do you secretly resist.
q3_5.subtitle: the ones you go along with publicly but quietly disagree with — about money, relationships, success, gender, anything

q3_6.title: What would your family or community disapprove of most about the real you.
q3_6.subtitle: the parts of yourself, your life, or your choices you keep hidden from them, and why you keep them hidden

q3_7.title: What kind of person were you expected to become.
q3_7.subtitle: the future others imagined for you — career, family, behaviour, image — before you had any say in it

q4_1.title: How many people truly know the real you.
q4_1.subtitle: the people who have seen the unedited version of you and would not be shocked by anything in your inner life

q4_2.title: In groups, you usually become.
q4_2.subtitle: the role you slide into without thinking — the funny one, the listener, the leader, the observer, the one who keeps things smooth

q4_3.title: How afraid are you of disappointing others.
q4_3.subtitle: how much another person's reaction — a look, a sigh, silence — can shape what you say or do

q4_4.title: What parts of yourself do you hide socially.
q4_4.subtitle: the thoughts, feelings, traits, or pieces of your history you keep tucked away when you are around other people

q4_5.title: When do you feel most accepted.
q4_5.subtitle: the situations or relationships where you stop performing and can just be — describe what makes those spaces different

q4_6.title: What social situations drain you most.
q4_6.subtitle: the gatherings, dynamics, or relationships that leave you more tired than they should — and what about them is exhausting

q4_7.title: What kind of people do you envy.
q4_7.subtitle: envy usually points at something you want but have not let yourself want openly — describe who triggers it and why

q5_1.title: Which platforms do you actively use.
q5_1.subtitle: the apps you open out of habit, more than once a day, not the ones you technically have an account on

q5_2.title: Average daily usage per platform.
q5_2.subtitle: a rough estimate of how much time you actually spend on each one — minutes or hours, no judgement

q5_3.title: What you mainly use them for.
q5_3.subtitle: the real reason underneath the obvious one — connection, distraction, validation, escape, comparison, information

q5_4.title: How often do you delete or edit posts before publishing.
q5_4.subtitle: how much you rehearse, second-guess, or rewrite what you share before letting other people see it

q5_5.title: How often do you compare your life to others online.
q5_5.subtitle: the quiet measuring that happens while scrolling — about looks, success, relationships, lifestyle, anything

q5_6.title: What version of yourself appears online.
q5_6.subtitle: describe the character you present — the curated version — and how it differs from who you are when no one is watching

q5_7.title: What do you seek emotionally when you open social media.
q5_7.subtitle: the feeling you are reaching for in the moment you open the app — distraction, comfort, excitement, numbness, connection

q5_8.title: What kind of content makes you uncomfortable.
q5_8.subtitle: the posts or videos that make you want to scroll past quickly, and what you think that discomfort is really about

q5_9.title: What kind of people attract your attention online.
q5_9.subtitle: the accounts you stop and watch — describe the qualities they share and what draws you in

q6_1.title: Your current relationship status.
q6_1.subtitle: where you actually are right now — single, dating, partnered, married, separated, complicated — not where you wish you were

q6_2.title: How many serious relationships have you been in.
q6_2.subtitle: the ones that mattered emotionally, regardless of how long they lasted or how official they were

q6_3.title: Typical conflicts in your relationships.
q6_3.subtitle: the arguments that keep showing up in different forms across different partners — money, distance, control, communication

q6_4.title: In relationships you tend to.
q6_4.subtitle: your default move when things get hard — pull closer, pull away, take charge, shut down, try to fix

q6_5.title: What kind of people do you repeatedly fall for.
q6_5.subtitle: the type that keeps appearing in your love life — not just looks, but emotional patterns, temperament, how they treat you

q6_6.title: What usually ends your relationships.
q6_6.subtitle: the real reason things fall apart, beyond the official story you tell friends or family

q6_7.title: What emotional need do you most want fulfilled.
q6_7.subtitle: the need you find hardest to ask for directly — being seen, being chosen, being safe, being free, being wanted

q6_8.title: What do you fear most in intimacy.
q6_8.subtitle: what closeness puts at risk for you — being known, being trapped, being left, being too much, being not enough

q7_1.title: Your current employment status.
q7_1.subtitle: the shape of your working life right now — employed, self-employed, between jobs, studying, caregiving, something else

q7_2.title: How satisfied are you with your career direction.
q7_2.subtitle: the longer arc of where your work is going, not how you feel about this particular week

q7_3.title: At work you are usually.
q7_3.subtitle: the way you operate professionally — the role you take when no one is assigning one to you

q7_4.title: Your biggest workplace stress.
q7_4.subtitle: the source of pressure that follows you home — a person, a workload, a fear, an environment, a pattern

q7_5.title: What does success emotionally mean to you.
q7_5.subtitle: the feeling you imagine arrives when you finally have it — relief, pride, peace, freedom, being enough

q7_6.title: What kind of recognition affects you most.
q7_6.subtitle: the praise that genuinely lands and changes how you feel, and the kind that bounces off no matter how much of it you get

q7_7.title: What failure still influences you today.
q7_7.subtitle: a specific failure you have not quite finished processing — what happened, and how it still shapes your choices

q7_8.title: If money disappeared, what would you pursue.
q7_8.subtitle: the work or activity you would do even if no one paid you for it — describe what it looks like

q8_1.title: How do you usually cope with stress.
q8_1.subtitle: what you reach for when things get heavy — food, screens, exercise, isolation, talking, substances, sleep, work

q8_2.title: How often do you go out socially.
q8_2.subtitle: how often you spend time with other people in person, not online or through messages

q8_3.title: How often do you feel lonely even in a group.
q8_3.subtitle: the loneliness that shows up when you are surrounded by people but still feel unseen or far away

q8_4.title: What activities make you forget yourself.
q8_4.subtitle: the things that pull you in so deeply that time disappears — for better or worse, healthy or not

q8_5.title: What do you avoid thinking about most.
q8_5.subtitle: the topic or memory you steer away from quickly when it comes up — about yourself, your past, your future

q8_6.title: When do you feel emotionally numb.
q8_6.subtitle: the situations where the volume drops to zero — work, relationships, conflict, intimacy, being alone

q8_7.title: What habit feels hardest to stop.
q8_7.subtitle: the behaviour you have tried more than once to change or quit, without success — describe what it is and what keeps pulling you back

q9_1.title: How self-critical are you.
q9_1.subtitle: the tone of your inner voice when you mess up or fall short — harsh, fair, dismissive, devastating

q9_2.title: Which statement feels closest to your private fear.
q9_2.subtitle: the sentence about yourself that lives underneath everything else, the one you would only admit on a hard day

q9_3.title: How often do you feel disconnected from yourself.
q9_3.subtitle: the sense of watching your own life from a small distance, like you are not fully inside it

q9_4.title: What thought repeats in your mind most often.
q9_4.subtitle: the looping sentence or worry that comes back regularly — write it in its actual words, not a summary

q9_5.title: What do you criticise yourself for privately.
q9_5.subtitle: the things you score yourself on that no one else knows about — about your body, mind, choices, character

q9_6.title: What would make you feel enough.
q9_6.subtitle: the condition you have quietly set for yourself to finally relax — be honest, the answer is often smaller than you expect

q9_7.title: If your inner voice had a personality, how would you describe it.
q9_7.subtitle: the age, gender, tone of that voice — and whose voice it might actually be, if you trace it back

q10_1.title: Which matters more to you.
q10_1.subtitle: pick the one that matters most right now — the others can still matter, but be honest about the ranking

q10_2.title: How hopeful are you about your future.
q10_2.subtitle: the felt sense when you think ahead, not the upbeat answer you give other people when they ask

q10_3.title: What do you secretly want most.
q10_3.subtitle: the want you have not quite let yourself name out loud — the one that feels too big, too risky, or too embarrassing

q10_4.title: Describe your ideal future life in detail.
q10_4.subtitle: the concrete details — where you are, who you are with, what your mornings look like, the work, the light, the rhythm

q10_5.title: What fear could destroy that future.
q10_5.subtitle: the thing — internal or external — that has stopped you before, and could stop you again if you let it

q10_6.title: What part of yourself are you still trying to become.
q10_6.subtitle: the version of you on the horizon — the qualities, the freedoms, the way of being you are slowly moving toward

q10_7.title: If nobody judged you, how would you live differently.
q10_7.subtitle: the choices you would make if the watching stopped — about work, love, body, time, money, voice

q10_8.title: What do you think you are truly searching for.
q10_8.subtitle: the deeper thing underneath all your previous answers — what every choice and longing is really pointing at

origins.title: Origins
origins.subtitle: developmental imprinting

headline: The first
bonds
, and the shape they left.
attachment.lede: Locates your attachment style, your relation to authority, and the triangulation you grew up inside. The shape of the first bond becomes the template every later one is measured against.
attachment.title: Attachment
attachment.subtitle: family structure

headline: The voices you
inherited
authority.lede: Surfaces the moral codes, guilt structures, and inherited identity still running in the background. The voices you grew up under rarely leave; they become the voice that judges you.
authority.title: Authority
authority.subtitle: symbolic law

headline: Who gets to
see you
belonging.lede: Measures social dependence, identity masking, and the fear of exclusion. Belonging is rarely free; this section asks what you trade for it.
belonging.title: Belonging
belonging.subtitle: social identity

headline: The self you
perform
persona.lede: Reads the idealised self, the validation loop, and the symbolic performance you stage online. The persona is not a lie; it is a half-revealed wish.
persona.title: Persona
persona.subtitle: desire & digital self

headline: The pattern that
keeps returning
desire.lede: Finds the recurring relational shape, the abandonment fear, the contradiction inside desire. What repeats is rarely chosen; it is what asks to be seen.
desire.title: Desire
desire.subtitle: intimacy & repetition

headline: What you are
trying to prove
achievement.lede: Detects achievement anxiety, recognition hunger, and your relation to authority at work. Underneath every ambition is an audience of one or two people.
achievement.title: Achievement
achievement.subtitle: work & recognition

headline: Where you go
to not be here
escape.lede: Identifies the avoidance patterns, the compulsions, and the rituals that regulate pleasure. The exit you reach for says as much as the room you leave.
escape.title: Escape
escape.subtitle: pleasure & ritual

headline: The voice you can't
quite quiet
self-relation.lede: Maps the superego's edge, the shame structures, and the internalised voices. The way you speak to yourself in private is the most honest record of who raised you.
self-relation.title: Self-relation
self-relation.subtitle: internal dialogue

headline: What you are
truly searching for
future-fantasy.lede: The emotional climax — the future you imagine, the fear that haunts it, the core desire underneath. The last question is the first one returned.
future-fantasy.title: Future-fantasy
future-fantasy.subtitle: fantasy, fear & desire
